All batches enter the same layer at the same time, so the bandwidth demand of memory-heavy layers (large weights, large activations) is aligned in time. The instantaneous DDR bandwidth requirement becomes roughly N × peak where N is the batch count. When this peak exceeds the available DDR bandwidth, the NPU stalls waiting for memory. In a multi-instance dp_size=1 configuration, each instance runs independently. Operating system thread scheduling naturally introduces minor phase offsets (sub-millisecond stagger) between instances.
